out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: dessert display at Little Villagio thermostat reading 41, but food in unit >41F; cold rail in Little Villagio reading 25F, but food in unit >41F.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: Permit to Operate Posted in Conspicuous Location
violations.observation: The establishment has not posted the permit to operate in a conspicuous location. Observed no 2026 food establishment permit posted.
violations.corrective_action: A valid permit shall be posted in every food establishment in a conspicuous place in the public view. Food establishment permits are issued for a calendar year and expire on December 31 regardless of the month of issue. Post 2026 food establishment permit. Contact [county email] for a copy.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: observed tray of raw chicken stored above cooked rice on speedrack in WIC.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CFM moved tray of raw chicken to bottom of rack.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Approved Device Provided
violations.observation: Observed the lack of an approved backflow prevention device on the water supply system. Observed unapproved splitter installed on mop sink faucet.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by installing an approved backflow prevention device as specified under 5-202.14. CFM removed unapproved spitter. EHS provided approved splitter options. CFM will send EHS picture of approved device installed.

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Shellstock Removed from Tagged or Labeled Container
violations.observation: Shellstock has been removed from the tagged/labeled container without preserving source identification. Observed shellstock in refrigeration units without tags in same container. CFM stated tags kept in separate area.
violations.corrective_action: Shellstock that has been removed from the tagged/labeled container must have a system used to identify source. EHS had CFM replace tags and educated CFM that tags must be kept with shellstock until last shellstock sold.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: scampi sauce, vodka sauce, pappardelle, spicy white wine sauce (mussel), pesto sauce, tomato, arugula, romaine, prosciutto, burrata, horseradish, green aioli.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to-eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. CFM had employee mark foods with 4 hour end point of 1530.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food
violations.observation: A review of the menu with the foodservice operator indicates that there is no consumer advisory for the following food item(s) that may be served raw and/or undercooked: salmon, steak, tuna add-on for salads on Little Villagio menu.
violations.corrective_action: If an animal food such as beef, eggs, fish, lamb, milk, pork, poultry, or shellfish is served or sold raw or undercooked the permit holder shall inform consumers of the significantly increased risk of consuming such foods by way of a disclosure and reminder using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means. CFM will update menu. EHS will follow up on or around 10 days to ensure menus are updated and food items are labelled properly with consumer advisory. TRATTORIA VILLAGIO (Inspection Date: 10/01/2025) Page 3 of 5

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: spray bottle with water at pizza station, squeeze bottles of oil along main cookline.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. CFM had employee label secondary containers with food name.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Controlling Pests, Pest Control Methods
violations.observation: Methods are not being used to control pests. Observed flies in back kitchen area of Little Villagio.
violations.corrective_action: Insects and other pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces. If pests are found on the premises methods shall be used to control their presence. EHS recommended requesting pest control services for flies.

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: Openings to the exterior of the building are present along the bottom edge of exit door in Little Villagio.
violations.corrective_action: Fill or close holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. EHS recommended installing/replacing door sweep to prevent potential pest entry.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: ice cream scoop in container of room temperature water.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. CFM discarded water in container. EHS reviewed proper in-use utensil storage.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Approved Device Provided
violations.observation: Observed the lack of an approved backflow prevention device on the water supply system. Observed unapproved splitter installed on mop sink faucet.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by installing an approved backflow prevention device as specified under 5-202.14. CFM agreed to remove unapproved splitter and contact chemical company to install approved splitter. CFM will provide proof of installation when work is complete.

out_items.name: Adequate ventilation and lighting, designated areas used

violations.title: Designated Storage for Clothing, Possessions
violations.observation: Observed employee clothing and other possessions stored in areas that may contaminate food, food-contact surfaces of equipment, single-service items, or single- use items. Observed employee personal belongings stored on shelf next to food items in pizza prep area.
violations.corrective_action: Instruct employees to use the designated lockers and clothes hooks to prevent contamination of food, food equipment and utensils, and preparation surfaces. CFM had employee move personal belongings away from food preparation area.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Chlorine Requirements
violations.observation: When tested, the low temperature, chemical sanitizing warewashing machine was observed with a sanitizing rinse concentration of less than 50 ppm chlorine solution: Observed at 0 ppm due to sanitizer bucket was empty.
violations.corrective_action: Immediately discontinue use of the dishmachine. Until the machine is adequately repaired, set up the three-compartment sink to manually wash, rinse and sanitize food-contact surfaces using a sanitizing solution at the proper concentration of at least 50 to 100 ppm total chlorine. CDI - New sanitizer bucket provided and connected to dish machine, retested at 100 ppm during inspection.

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Surfaces of ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment are not being cleaned as required: Observed accumulation of debris inside ice machine.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Poison/Toxic Material, Application
violations.observation: Observed hanging pesticide strips in several locations above storage items and equipment throughout the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Hazardous and toxic materials shall be applied in such a way that prevents the contamination of food and food contact surfaces. CDI - EHS instructed staff to relocate these below shelves or under sinks where no equipment/food is stored.
